item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
Harvard University’s Opportunity Insights (OI), is seeking applicants for a Data Scientist.

Opportunity Insights (OI) is a nonpartisan research and policy institute focused on improving economic opportunity. Founded in 2018, Opportunity Insight has become a nationally- and internationally- recognized leader in the science of economic mobility and in the use of large administrative data to understand and address inequality. Opportunity Insights has published seminal work on national trends in upward mobility; racial disparities; the role of neighborhoods, social capital, and higher education in upward mobility; the use of private-sector data to understand disparate impacts in the recent economic recession and recovery; and new methods to estimate program impacts. To complement this research, Opportunity Insights has developed data resources including the Opportunity Atlas, the Social Capital Atlas, and the Economic Tracker to support evidence-based policy and practice. To date, OI’s work has shaped policy discussions at the national and local level, with nearly a dozen of its studies covered on the front pages of major media outlets, such as the New York Times, The Economist, the Wall Street Journal, and have been widely cited in policy discussions, including the President’s State of the Union address.

The Data Scientist will have two responsibilities. The first is to conduct economic and statistical analysis to support evidence-based investments and cost-benefit evaluation to promote economic mobility. The person in this role will design and implement statistical and econometric models to estimate program impacts, develop financial models of returns to program investments, and conduct cost-benefit and impact analyses. The second objective is to translate findings from these analyses and other ongoing research at Opportunity Insights into actionable insights for external stakeholders and the broader public, ranging from policymakers to students participating in OI’s new data science courses. Both sets of activities will be conducted in collaboration with other current members of the Opportunity Insights team.

Term: This is a two-year term position with a strong possibility of renewal.

Location: The position is located in Cambridge, MA, with the possibility of hybrid work arrangements.

Compensation and Benefits: Harvard’s salary grades and ranges can be found here. This position is classified at level 59. We invite you to visit Harvard’s Total Rewards website here to learn more about Harvard’s benefits package.

The individual taking on this role will be responsible for the following:

Policy Evaluation and Financial Modeling

  • Lead efforts to acquire, clean, and manage large administrative and program datasets.

  • Design and conduct econometric studies assessing the effectiveness of public policies, social programs, and other mobility-related interventions.

  • Apply causal inference methods including matching estimators, quasi-experimental designs, and other techniques.

  • Model financial returns from alternative portfolios of investments, including expected returns and risk assessment.

  • Ensure methodological rigor and transparency in all analyses.

Cost-Benefit Analysis and Tool Development

  • Conduct cost-benefit analyses (CBA) to estimate returns of programs.

  • Quantify direct and indirect economic and social benefits.

  • Develop a calculator to estimate cost savings and impacts of state and federal tax revenues.

  • Integrate findings into dashboards, reports, and visualizations for internal decision-makers and external partners.

Teaching and Mentoring

  • Support OI initiatives to teach data science and OI research to high school and college students.

  • Supervise and collaborate with junior analysts and predoctoral research assistants as needed.

  • Provide technical guidance on modeling, interpretation, and quality assurance.

  • Contribute to internal capacity building and knowledge-sharing across teams.

Communication of Results

  • Produce technical reports summarizing results for relevant internal and external stakeholders.

  • Help prepare non-technical policy briefs, reports, and presentations summarizing key findings, uncertainties, and implications.

  • Represent the organization in briefings, conferences, and stakeholder meetings.

BACKGROUND/EXPERIENCE

  • Ph.D. in Economics, Public Policy, Statistics, or related field.

  • Minimum 2 years of professional experience in applied econometric analysis, preferably in policy evaluation, government, or academic settings.

SPECIFIC JOB SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES

  • Expertise in:

    • Causal inference and econometric modeling

    • Analysis of big data

    • Cost-benefit analysis

    • Quantitative impact evaluation and forecasting

    • Writing technical and non-technical economics papers

    • Programming languages such as R, Stata, Python, and SAS

  • Proven ability to translate technical results into actionable policy insights.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting to nontechnical audiences.

  • Experience and interest in working in collaborative settings with other team members.

How to Apply

Please apply through Harvard’s online portal. To be considered for this position, a cover letter and resume/CV must be submitted. A skills assessment may be required as part of the interview process. Should you have questions, please contact hiring@opportunityinsights.org.

EEO/Non-Discrimination Commitment Statement

Harvard University is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination. We seek talent from all parts of society and the world, and we strive to ensure everyone at Harvard thrives. Our differences help our community advance Harvard’s academic purposes. Harvard has an equal employment opportunity policy that outlines our commitment to prohibiting discrimination on the basis of race, ethnicity, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, religion, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law or identified in the university’s non-discrimination policy. item.description: The Economics Team is the nexus of economics at EDF, ensuring that the economic thinking that is the backbone for all EDF policy positions is based on the best available research and information.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Economics Team is the nexus of economics at EDF, ensuring that the economic thinking that is the backbone for all EDF policy positions is based on the best available research and information. To be most effective in this role, the Office of the Chief Economist provides support for other teams throughout EDF and fosters relationships with economists outside the organization.

Overall Function

The Senior Analyst, Economics & Policy Analysis will be a key member of the Economics Team through a two-year fixed-term contract. In the first year, this position will support research and analysis focused on methane emissions from the oil and gas industry, with an emphasis on advancing EDF’s Global Methane Initiative priorities. In the second year, the role will transition to support the Economic Analysis Hub (Hub) team, contributing to analysis for other initiatives across EDF. This position will report to the Director, Economics & Policy, or to the Director, Economic Analysis Hub.

In the first year, this Senior Analyst, Economics & Policy Analysis will support EDF’s cross-programmatic Global Methane Initiative by providing critical research and analysis to reduce methane emissions in North America and other major oil and gas producing regions. This Senior Analyst will support research to understand why wells become orphaned and critically assess policies designed to reduce the burden of orphan and idle wells. In addition, the senior analyst will be involved in efforts to seek reforms in law, regulation, and/or business practice through a set of strategic corporate partnerships, direct engagement with policymakers, and mobilizing investors and public sentiment in favor of change. Finally, the senior analyst will also support efforts to inform EDF’s Global Methane advocacy goals through the lens of economic principles, and by coordinating our work with an external network of researchers and economists.

In the second year, the role will transition to serve as a member of the Economic Analysis Hub (Hub) team, a unit at EDF that conducts rapid analysis of climate economics questions to inform organizational priorities, decision makers, and policy needs. While the Senior Analyst will leverage their expertise on oil and gas methane in this role, their role on the Hub will expand their responsibilities to include work on other topics as needed. This role offers exposure to other high-impact work, with contributions that can influence congressional testimony and international climate negotiations.

Responsibilities

  • Under general supervision, take a lead role in responding to rapid-turnaround analytical requests from the Economics, Global Methane, and Hub teams, translating technical findings into clear insights for policy and advocacy needs.

  • Build and maintain knowledge on a variety of topics related to EDF’s Global Methane work, including oil and gas methane regulations and policy design, energy policy developments in key jurisdictions with a focus on North America, well-level oil and gas production trends, orphaned and idle wells, the social cost of methane.

  • As the role transitions to the Economic Analysis Hub, conduct research on climate economics topics, including carbon pricing mechanisms, clean energy transitions, risk and resilience, and the economic impacts of environmental policies in response to requests from EDF program teams.

  • Perform literature reviews on methane emissions, oil and gas policy design, economic modeling methodologies, climate policy evaluations, and emerging topics in environmental economics.

  • Process and validate large-scale oil and gas datasets (e.g., Enverus) and economic datasets (e.g. national accounts, energy systems, emissions inventories, etc.).

  • Assess and document model inputs, assumptions, performance, and methodological choices, and develop reproducible data pipelines to support transparency, quality assurance, reproducibility, and rapid policy response.

  • Author and co-author written materials including public comments, white papers, memos, and policy briefs; clearly summarize research for technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Represent EDF to external audiences in both formal settings (e.g., conference presentations) and informal settings (e.g., check-in meetings with external partners).

  • Engage with stakeholders and academic partners including responding to inquiries and soliciting subject matter expertise.

  • Participates in advancing EDF Organizational Effectiveness and Culture (OEC) Goals in which people from all backgrounds and experiences feel connected, included, and empowered to address the environmental and organizational challenges in alignment with EDF values.

Qualifications

We are seeking candidates who have demonstrated ability to conduct rigorous research and analysis in the area of environmental policy, economics, or a closely related field. Candidates must have exceptional problem-solving skills, work independently, and be able to ensure consistency and quality of research products. Candidates should also have:

  • A Master’s-level degree in economics, environment and energy policy, or a closely related field or at least two years’ relevant experience.

  • Knowledge of climate change and energy systems and ability to apply economic principles and methods to these systems.

  • High degree of proficiency in data analysis software, including R and/or Python.

  • Excellent written and oral communication skills; including the ability to prepare written materials for a variety of audiences and present research to internal and external audiences.

  • Ability to perform complex research and analysis in support of highly visible work

  • Experience taking initiative and working independently to manage research projects and participate in research efforts, and in ensuring consistency and quality of research products.

  • Demonstrates self-awareness, cultural competency and inclusivity, and ability to work with colleagues and stakeholders across all cultures and backgrounds.

  • Ability to support a multi-disciplinary team, using independent judgment required to plan, prioritize, and organize a diversified workload.

  • Experience with project management and creating workplans that bring together deliverables, timelines and contributors.

  • Consistent willingness to take initiative, lead projects, and multi-task under tight deadlines.

We offer a strong total rewards package encompassing competitive salary, robust benefits, and professional development opportunities consistent with a modern global organization. We take into account factors such as candidate experience, skills, training, internal team equity and local norms.

Please note that pay ranges are country specific. As a result, the stated currency is not meant be converted into any other currency.

Location

Remote US-Home or Hybrid (Boulder or Washington, D.C. preferred).

Duration

This is a 2-year fixed-term position with full benefits and the possibility of extension.

Application Instructions

Please include a cover letter indicating your interest in this role. Also, please submit a 2-3 page writing sample that illustrates the application of an economic theory or framework to a real-world problem. You may submit an excerpt from existing work (such as a paper, thesis chapter, or policy memo).

Your sample should:

  • Clearly identify the real-world problem or question you’re addressing

  • Show how a specific economic theory or framework helps explain or analyze it.

You may not use AI to craft or assist with the analysis or writing. We are most interested in seeing how you reason through a problem and communicate your analysis. If you’re submitting an excerpt, please include one or two sentences of context so we can follow it without the full document. If the sample was co-authored, please note your specific contribution.

item.content:encoded:
The IDB Group is a community of diverse, versatile, and passionate people who come together on a journey to improve lives in Latin America and the Caribbean. Our people find purpose and do what they love in an inclusive, collaborative, agile, and rewarding environment.

About this position

We are looking for a rigorous, innovative, and driven Economist Specialist . As an Economist, you will conduct cutting-edge applied economic research, generate high-impact empirical evidence, and provide technical guidance to shape public policies across Latin America and the Caribbean.

You will work in the Institutions for Development Sector (IFD) in the Vice Presidency for Sectors and Knowledge. This team is responsible for designing, supporting, and executing analytical and operational agendas that strengthen public sector governance, state capacity, digital transformation, citizen security and crime prevention, and efficient financial markets.

What you’ll do

  • Conduct high-level empirical research in public economics, applied microeconomics, and development economics, focusing on citizen security, state capacity, digitalization, and financial markets.

  • Lead and contribute to flagship institutional publications, research papers, and policy notes produced by the sector, devoting at least 60% of professional time to research activities.

  • Support the Sectoral Economic Advisor (SEA) in managing, coordinating, and ensuring the quality of research and analytical products across IFD divisions, acting as a key technical resource to support the broader department in knowledge matters under the SEA’s direction.

  • Work closely with the network of knowledge coordinators across divisions to review, comment on, and provide continuous technical feedback on analytical outputs and departmental knowledge initiatives.

  • Assist in preparing responses to Vice Presidency for Sectors (VPS) and Vice Presidency for Countries (VPC) requests, ensuring rigorous technical and economic backing.

  • Provide technical assistance and economic analysis for regional and country operations, technical cooperations, and policy dialogues related to state modernization and financial development.

  • Design and execute empirical evaluations, randomized controlled trials, and econometric modeling using administrative and survey data to measure the impact of public interventions.

  • Collaborate with internal colleagues, external academic networks, and multilateral partners to advance the sector’s strategic research agenda.

  • Disseminate research findings through academic seminars, policy forums, workshops, and peer-reviewed international journals.

  • Support institutional knowledge management initiatives, training sessions, and technical workshops organized by the sector.

  • Perform other institutional and analytical tasks assigned by the Sectoral Economic Advisor to support the production, management, and dissemination of knowledge.

What you’ll need

• Education: Masters degree required, PhD in Economics, Public Policy, or a closely related field strongly preferred

• Experience: At least 4 years (5 preferably) of progressive professional experience in empirical research, policy analysis, or economic development, with a strong publication record or pipeline in applied microeconomics or public economics.

• Languages: Proficiency in Spanish and English, spoken and written, is required. Additional knowledge of French and Portuguese is preferable.

Requirements

• Citizenship: You are a citizen of one of our 48-member countries. We may offer assistance with relocation and visa applications for you and your eligible dependents.

• Consanguinity: You have no family members (up to the fourth degree of consanguinity and second degree of affinity, including spouse) working at the IDB, IDB Invest, or IDB Lab.

Type of contract and duration

• Staff: International staff contract, 36 months initially, renewable upon mutual agreement.

What we offer

The IDB group provides benefits that respond to the different needs and moments of an employee’s life. These benefits include:

  • A competitive compensation package, including an annual base salary expressed on a net-of-tax basis.

  • Leaves and vacations: 24 days of paid time off + 8 personal days + sick leave + gender-neutral parental leave.

  • Health Insurance: IDB Group provides employees and eligible dependents with a robust medical benefits program that covers medical, dental, vision, preventive care, and prescription drugs.

  • Pension plan: defined benefit pension plan that provides financial security and support employees in planning for their future.

  • We offer assistance with relocation and visa applications for you and your family when it applies.

  • On-site position with the occasional flexibility of teleworking.

  • Health and well-being: Access to our Health Services Center that provides preventive care and health education for employees.

  • Development support: We offer tools to boost your professional profile, such as mentoring, 1:1 professional counseling, training and learning opportunities, language classes, mobility options, among others.

  • Other office amenities (as available): Lactation Room, Daycare Center, Gym, Bike Racks, Parking, spouse career support, and others.

Our culture

At the IDB, we work so everyone brings their best and authentic selves to work while finding their purpose. Our people consistently strive for excellence, and we recognize and celebrate the impact of their contributions.

In our efforts to drive innovation, we intentionally include all voices, cultivate a sense of belonging and champion fairness. We welcome individuals from underrepresented groups to join us and share their unique perspectives.

We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job interview process. If you require an accommodation to complete this application, please email us at accommodations@iadb.org.
